item.title: The consultant you need is already on campus
item.description: Agne Rimkute explains what an MBA student revealed about impact, data, and how fragmented student support can become – and why universities and their SUs can harness their insights

item.title: Do students lack skills, or does the system struggle to surface them?
item.description: Jim Dickinson considers whether concerns about graduate readiness reflect missing attributes – or a system that fails to surface and record what students have already learned

item.title: Higher education postcard: big science
item.description: This week’s card from Hugh Jones’ postbag takes us to a research facility which really stands out

item.title: HESA Spring 2026: Staff
item.description: In times of turmoil and upheaval in the sector what's happening with full-time academic staff numbers? As David Kernohan explains, the picture is more complex than you may expect

item.title: Whole-of-society defence needs an alliance that universities actually own
item.description: For Tom Smith, the new Defence Universities Alliance must not just be a branding exercise with universities as a convenient subcontractor

item.title: If the graduate premium is falling, supply-side tinkering won’t bring it back
item.description: Jim Dickinson assembles cross-national evidence showing Britain's shrinking graduate premium is a demand-side problem – and that closing courses won't fix it

item.title: Here’s what happens when you start AI policy with values, not tools
item.description: At Royal Holloway, the creation of an AI policy became a moment of profound reflection on institutional ethics and purpose. Lucy Gill-Simmen and Will Will Shüler elaborate

item.title: Safeguarding the art of lecturing in an AI age
item.description: Students are using AI as a personal tutor, but AI is using materials prepared by academics in order to do this. Shonagh Douglas and Lisa Collie ask who is looking after the interests of academics here?

item.title: Learning community means even more in the age of AI
item.description: Debbie McVitty posits that human interaction matters in learning not because it's "better" but simply because it's human

item.title: Educating for humans in the lead
item.description: Mark Peace posits that our anxiety about the threats of AI to standards risk blinding us to a deeper need to reassert the value of humanness in knowledge work
